question.text: Body diffusion-weighted MR imaging of uterine endometrial cancer: is it helpful in the detection of cancer in nonenhanced MR imaging?
question.context: In this study, the authors discussed the feasibility and value of diffusion-weighted (DW) MR imaging in the detection of uterine endometrial cancer in addition to conventional nonenhanced MR images. DW images of endometrial cancer in 23 patients were examined by using a 1.5-T MR scanner. This study investigated whether or not DW images offer additional incremental value to conventional nonenhanced MR imaging in comparison with histopathological results. Moreover, the apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) values were measured in the regions of interest within the endometrial cancer and compared with those of normal endometrium and myometrium in 31 volunteers, leiomyoma in 14 patients and adenomyosis in 10 patients. The Wilcoxon rank sum test was used, with a p<0.05 considered statistically significant. In 19 of 23 patients, endometrial cancers were detected only on T2-weighted images. In the remaining 4 patients, of whom two had coexisting leiomyoma, no cancer was detected on T2-weighted images. This corresponds to an 83% detection sensitivity for the carcinomas. When DW images and fused DW images/T2-weighted images were used in addition to the T2-weighted images, cancers were identified in 3 of the remaining 4 patients in addition to the 19 patients (overall detection sensitivity of 96%). The mean ADC value of endometrial cancer (n=22) was (0.97+/-0.19)x10(-3)mm(2)/s, which was significantly lower than those of the normal endometrium, myometrium, leiomyoma and adenomyosis (p<0.05).

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that diffusion-weighted MR imaging (DW MRI) significantly improves the detection of uterine endometrial cancer compared to nonenhanced MR imaging alone. The addition of DW images increased the detection sensitivity from 83% to 96%.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: The addition of DW images and fused DW images/T2-weighted images increased the detection sensitivity from 83% to 96%.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While other conditions can affect the ADC value, the significant difference in ADC values between endometrial cancer and normal tissues strongly supports the utility of DW MRI for cancer detection. Other conditions like leiomyoma and adenomyosis were considered, but the significantly lower ADC value in endometrial cancer makes it the most relevant differential.

rnj1_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that diffusion-weighted (DW) MR imaging significantly improved the detection of endometrial cancer compared to conventional nonenhanced MR imaging alone. With DW and fused DW/T2 images, the detection sensitivity increased from 83% to 96%, indicating that DW imaging provides valuable additional information for identifying cancers that may be missed on T2-weighted images. The statistically significant lower ADC values in cancer compared to normal tissues further support the diagnostic utility of DW imaging.
rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: The 96% detection sensitivity when using DW and fused DW/T2 images compared to 83% with T2-weighted images alone demonstrates the incremental value of DW imaging in detecting endometrial cancer.
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: While other conditions like leiomyoma and adenomyosis were studied, the significant difference in ADC values between cancer and these benign conditions (p<0.05) confirms DW imaging's specificity in distinguishing cancer from non-cancerous lesions.

qwen3_vl_8b.clinical_reasoning: The study demonstrates that diffusion-weighted (DW) imaging significantly improved detection sensitivity from 83% (T2-only) to 96% (T2 + DW), identifying cancers missed on T2-weighted images. This incremental value, supported by statistically significant lower ADC values in cancer vs. normal tissues, confirms DW imaging adds diagnostic utility beyond nonenhanced MR.
qwen3_vl_8b.critical_evidence: DW images identified 3 of the 4 cancers missed on T2-weighted images, increasing overall sensitivity to 96%, with ADC values significantly lower in cancer (p<0.05).
qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Leiomyoma and adenomyosis were considered differentials but were excluded by ADC values; their higher ADC values distinguished them from cancer, supporting DW's specificity and incremental value.

olmo3_7b.differential_considered: Other benign uterine lesions (leiomyoma, adenomyosis) had higher ADC values than the endometrial cancer, so DW imaging helps distinguish cancer from these mimics. However, DW MRI is not a standalone diagnostic tool but is most helpful when used in combination with conventional imaging.
